fields.meta_title: Influencer Application Form Builder for Brands | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an influencer application form that collects handles, follower counts, and rates, then sends each applicant to the right person. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Influencer Application Form That Sorts Every Applicant
fields.hero_description: Build an influencer application form that saves each creator's handles, audience, and rate in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Everything Needed to Say Yes to a Creator
fields.features_subheading: An influencer application form built in Emergent collects the details to check before you send product or pay a rate.
fields.feature_1:
One row for each platform

Applicants add a row for every platform they post on, with the handle and the follower count side by side. A creator on Instagram and TikTok fills in two rows, not one crowded box.
fields.feature_2:
Media kits and sample posts as uploads

Ask for a media kit and links to three recent sponsored posts. The files are saved with the application, so the reviewer sees past work without emailing the creator to ask for it.
fields.feature_3:
A rate field with a ceiling you set

Ask for a rate per deliverable, such as one Reel or one Story. A rate above the ceiling goes to a named approver by email or in Slack, and the rest go to the shortlist.
fields.feature_4:
Dates with a fixed number of spots

Offer hosted dates or event slots, each with a set number of creator spots. The form hides a date once its last spot is taken, so a full date never shows to the next applicant.
fields.feature_5:
Disclosure terms signed in the form

Close the form with your disclosure and usage terms and a typed or drawn signature. The signed terms are stored with the date and the application, in a database you own.
fields.feature_6:
Code a developer can take further

Export the code for the form and its review screens to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can host it on your own servers or keep building on it from there.
fields.why_title: Why Build Influencer Applications With Emergent?
fields.why_description: Pitches scattered across DMs lose the follower count and the rate. An application keeps both on one record you can sort and approve.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Brands Act on Each Application
fields.tab_content_1:
One seeding list, made from approved applications

Mossgrove Skincare ships a box of new products to a few creators each month. Mirela Szabo applies with 14,200 Instagram followers, combination skin, and a shipping address. Tamsin Okoro approves her, and the address moves to the March seeding list that Tamsin packs boxes from.
fields.tab_content_2:
The director signs off on any rate over $1,500

Strideline Running pays creators for its spring campaign, so every application asks for a rate. Teodor Lisk asks $2,400 for 1 Reel and 2 Stories and attaches his media kit. Any rate over $1,500 goes to Eloise Varga, the marketing director, by email before anyone replies to him.
fields.tab_content_3:
A weekend closes when its second creator applies

Pelican Rock Inn hosts 2 travel creators per weekend in return for coverage of the stay. Anouk Bastien takes the second spot on the November 14 weekend and reports that 58% of her audience is in the US. The form stops offering that weekend, and Hollis Tran gets her application in Slack.
fields.tab_content_4:
The signed #ad terms come back with the application

Kestrel Hill Tea ends its application with its terms: #ad in the caption of every post, and 90 days of paid usage for each video. Wilhelmina Oduya signs them with a drawn signature. When Briar Okonkwo opens the application, the signed terms and their date sit above the approve button.

plan.angle: The results for an influencer application form are template galleries that stop at name, handle and follower count. This page shows what a brand does with each application once it arrives: a skincare brand that ships seeding boxes to approved applicants, a running brand that routes high rates to its director, an inn that fills hosted weekends without overbooking, and a tea company that collects signed disclosure and usage terms before a post goes live, with the FTC's disclosure guidance stated from its own words.
tab_stories: Mirela Szabo applies to Mossgrove Skincare's seeding program with 14,200 Instagram followers and combination skin, and on approval her shipping address joins the March seeding list that Tamsin Okoro packs from.

Teodor Lisk applies to Strideline Running's spring campaign asking $2,400 for 1 Reel and 2 Stories, and because any rate over $1,500 goes to the marketing director, the application lands with Eloise Varga.

Anouk Bastien applies for a hosted weekend at Pelican Rock Inn, takes the second of 2 creator spots on the November 14 weekend, and Hollis Tran sees her application with a 58% US audience while that weekend closes on the form.

Wilhelmina Oduya's application to Kestrel Hill Tea ends with its terms, #ad in the caption of every post and 90 days of paid usage, which she signs, so Briar Okonkwo approves an application that already carries the signed terms.
